title: Fanout primer mismatch causes per-tenant tokens/sec collapse; emergency reconciliation and backstop rate-limiter
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Several enterprise customers on Dedicated and Private reported a sharp drop in tokens/sec and severe TTFT regressions after a recent primer allocation change. Impact: Hosted traffic saw elevated latencies for short-chat flows and Dedicated pools experienced tenant-local throughput collapse during fanout-heavy workloads. Root cause hypothesis: a mismatch between the fanout primer accounting and the per-tenant rate-limiter/eviction heuristics caused ephemeral warmup credits to be double-counted for some requests and omitted for others, triggering a cascade where prioritized primers starved regular token buckets. The mismatch surfaced only for models with heterogeneous context-window fallback variants (quantized + full-precision) and for sessions that triggered cross-variant fanout (probing variants for quality).

Observed behavior:
- Tokens/sec for affected tenants dropped by ~60% during peak minutes; TTFT increased by 2.5x for short prompts (<=128 tokens)
- Spike correlated with rollout of primer-reservation change in runtime-1.24 (PR #7892)
- Root-cause traces show primer credits being applied to transient hedged probes but not removed from tenant quota on probe completion

Goals:
1) Stabilize customer-facing throughput within SLO (tokens/sec >= 90% baseline) ASAP
2) Patch runtime to reconcile primer accounting and stop double consuming warmup credits
3) Add backstop rate-limiter to prevent cascading starvation during probes
4) Post-incident: add unit/integration tests and telemetry to detect primer-quota divergence

Immediate mitigation applied (2026-03-12):
- Rolled back primer-reservation change on canary hosts (region-us-central) which recovered tokens/sec to ~95% for canary tenants
- Enabled emergency backoff on probe fanout to cap probe concurrency per tenant (temporary config flag: runtime.probe_cap=2)

Planned fix (steps):
A) Hotfix: reconcile primer reservation lifecycle (1. patch accounting to decrement tenant warmup credits when probe finishes or is hedged; 2. ensure failure paths also decrement). Target: patch branch runtime-1.24-hotfix-primer. Owner: Diego.
B) Add a defensive per-tenant backstop token-bucket that cannot be fully drained by probes; probes should be charged to a separate ephemeral bucket with a hard floor. Owner: Lina Chen.
C) Add e2e test simulating cross-variant fanout with mixed quantized kernels to reproduce the divergence. Owner: QA team.
D) Instrumentation: add primer-to-quota reconciliation metric and a reconciliation alert when counts diverge >5% for any tenant for >2m. Owner: Observability.
E) Rollout plan: staged deploy to canaries -> 10% -> 50% -> all, with probe_cap enforced until metrics stable for 30m.

Rollback plan:
- If hotfix causes unexpected regressions, revert to previous runtime-1.24 canary binaries and keep probe_cap=2 until a corrected build is validated.

Verification criteria:
- Tokens/sec per-tenant back to >=90% of pre-incident baseline across Hosted/Dedicated/Private within 30m of rollout
- TTFT for short prompts returns to baseline within 30m
- Reconciliation metric shows zero divergence for 1 hour post-rollout

Notes on customer communication:
- CS notified major customers (AcmeHealth, VaultSuite) and provided mitigations and ETA. We committed to a 4-hour mitigation window and a follow-up postmortem.
- Drafted customer-facing incident note for Status page and customer success teams.

Risks and trade-offs:
- Introducing ephemeral probe buckets increases memory/slot usage under heavy fanout; mitigated by limiting probe concurrency and evicting stale probe entries after 10s
- Defensive rate-limiter may increase latency for some diagnostic probes; prioritized for stability

Local repro instructions:
1) Run model variant fanout harness (tools/fanout_harness) with a mix of quantized/FP variants for the same model family and enable hedged probing
2) Simulate multi-tenant traffic by starting 50 tenant sessions with short prompts (<=128 tokens) at 50 RPS
3) Observe primer_count vs tenant_quota via /debug/primer_metrics

Attach runbooks and references: see attachments

Next steps (owners):
- Diego: land runtime-1.24-hotfix-primer PR and coordinate canary rollout (target 2026-03-15 09:00 UTC)
- Lina Chen: implement backstop bucket and ensure probe charging semantics (target 2026-03-16)
- Observability: create reconciliation alert and dashboard tile (target 2026-03-15)
- QA: add deterministic e2e test mentioning mixed quant kernels (target 2026-03-18)

Postmortem TODOs:
- Root cause writeup and timeline
- Action items: test coverage, stricter probe accounting, and runtime invariants
- Review rollout automation to allow emergency probe_cap flag toggles per region
